fields.title: Parameter name
fields.description: A name for the input parameter (preferably unique). This name is exposed in the REST interface. It must start with a letter, followed by letters and digits and single minus signs or dashes and must end with a letter. Pattern: <tt>^[a-zA-Z](?:[-_]?[a-zA-Z0-9]+)*(?<![0-9])$</tt>

fields.title: Append unique ID to parameter name
fields.description: If checked, the name set above will be amended by the node's ID "{Parameter Name}-{Relative node ID}" to guarantee unique parameter names. Usually it's a good idea to have this box not checked and instead make sure to use meaningful and unique names in all container nodes present in a workflow.

fields.title: Description
fields.description: The description for the input parameter. It is currently not shown in the API specification of the REST interface but it's used for example when using this workflow as a tool for an AI Agent or when extracting the workflow summary.

fields.title: Input validation mode
fields.description: Controls whether the external input is validated against a configured template row specification.

fields.title: Set first row of input as template
fields.description:
By selecting this button, the first row of the input table, given one is provided, will be set as the new template row.
The template row defines the expected column names and types of the external input and the order of the output. It also populates the "InputParameters" field of the generated OpenAPI specification, which is presented to end users for documentation purposes.
When the node is executed without receiving any external input and has no table connected to its optional input port, the template row is used as the output.

fields.title: Missing values
fields.description: Defines how missing values in the input row are handled when validating against the template:

fields.title: Missing columns
fields.description:
Defines how missing columns, i.e. columns that the template requires but are not present in the input,
are handled:
